cli.build: python3 experiments/vm_observability/observe.py build --prepared DIR --out NEW_DIR --compiler PATH --sdk PATH --library PATH --deps DIR
cli.gate: Build/collect must be the COMMAND of W4 run_job.py; only prepare/offline audit/lightweight Python allowed before W4 ready; no timing command supplied

parameters.case: one of fixed case_ids; each process starts a fresh recorder
parameters.output: fresh directory only; never overwrite evidence

estimated: Core vector logical erase movement from element count; not machine memmove bytes
local: POSIX runtime only; Windows probes unavailable
sampled: lock wait/hold timings perturbed by probes
explicit owner capacity snapshots; allocator request ledger provides observed concurrent live requested-byte totals

event_json.bytes: requested/completed logical byte extent, or lock wait nanoseconds
event_json.copy_events: completed explicit memcpy/memmove/memset request bytes; vector_relocated_element counts logical completed element extent and is not recursive physical-copy accounting
event_json.host_allocate: completed backend allocator request; bytes=n*sizeof(rebound T), subject=allocation pointer, value=domain; allocator overhead/RSS excluded
event_json.host_deallocate: recorded BEFORE backend release to order address reuse; origin owner/domain/bytes taken from matched allocation pointer ledger
event_json.kind_catalog: event_kinds.json; exact allowlist and per-kind owner/subject/bytes/value legality; unknown kinds fail closed
event_json.lock_events: registry_lock or pool_lock; subject=mutex; bytes=wait_ns,value=hold_ns; diagnostic probe cost included
event_json.os_events: actual POSIX map/replace/protect/enable/discard/unmap calls with success/fail classification and requested bytes; injected rejection before syscall is a separate semantic input
event_json.overflow: fixed storage overflow or thread exhaustion sets valid=false,dropped>0; reject for interpretation
event_json.owner: per-kind identity in event_kinds.json: arena base for allocator/container costs, C++ object address for registry operations, causal Scope/0 for shared allocations/locks; never group mixed identities without kind
event_json.phase: static phase name assigned by caller; default unscoped
event_json.registry_events: owner=C++ XBufferCore object identity, subject=arena base; generation is successful registry_register sequence, ends registry_erase; registry_rebind changes object mapping within generation
event_json.sequence: globally unique consecutive integers 1..N ordered recorder observations; not proof of physical simultaneous allocator peaks
event_json.subject: uint64 allocation pointer, mutex pointer or event-specific address; 0 when not applicable
event_json.thread: recorder slot index, no claim of OS tid
event_json.value: event-specific dimensionless count/flag, allocation domain, old extent or lock hold nanoseconds

binary_roles.F_formal_timing: W3 separately built uninstrumented consumer; not supplied by W2
binary_roles.n3_diagnostic: generated F diagnostic only, N3_DIAGNOSTIC=1; never formal timing
binary_roles.n3_original: pristine F semantic comparator only, N3_DIAGNOSTIC=0; harness may contain clocks in unused recorder, NOT certified formal timing

identity.binding: prepared manifest binds contract+coverage+event catalog+generator+runtime+harness+N5 generator+both original/generated headers; build binds prepared result/commands/compiler/dependency/runtime/binary hashes; collection binds build result/binary hashes/raw stdout and recomputed summaries
identity.build: record compiler binary hash/version, dependency commits, runtime identities, exact commands, original and diagnostic binary hashes; diagnostic=true/timing_evidence=false
identity.evidence: completion marker hashes result manifest; raw stdout retained; offline audit recomputes counts and checks event order, allocation lifetimes, registration balance and deterministic case invariants
identity.prepare: verify both exact F header hashes; freeze pristine and generated headers, runtime, harness and imported N5 generator; record every anchor and resulting hashes

integration: W3 may build its own diagnostic program using frozen generated headers and runtime. Maintain original-F timing build separately; wrap phases explicitly, collect after join and audit trace. W2 tests are diagnostic semantics only, not D/F attribution or network timing.

probe_json.semantic: case-specific deterministic values; original-F and instrumented builds must agree
probe_json.status: passed for 9 ordinary cases; passed_control for recorder_overflow only
probe_json.trace: n3-events-v1; ordinary builds emit null; diagnostic builds emit event object

recorder_api.include: include frozen n3_runtime.hpp before frozen generated headers; header-only fixed zero-initialized process-lifetime recorder; no reset
recorder_api.invalid: thread/record/label overflow invalidates whole trace; recorder_overflow is only a negative control and contributes no interpretable costs
recorder_api.join_dump: join all workers, end relevant owned lifetimes, then n3::dump(std::ostream&); no emitting work may overlap dump
recorder_api.owner_scope: n3::Scope(base) supplies causal arena identity for shared allocation/OS/lock paths; nullptr resets to unowned; generated header supplies local scopes where available

workload_audit.custom_W3: supported structural trace/allocator/registry audit via audit_events.validate_trace(trace), plus W3 workload-specific preregistered semantic/resource checks; not certified by fixed-probe case assertions
workload_audit.end: quiescent dump may retain registered owners, pool slots/state and registry bucket allocations. Structural audit reports active/outstanding state instead of forcing zero. W3 must preregister exact permitted retained resource classes/counts/bounds and check them; fixed probes require no active owners and only shared registry buckets may remain.
workload_audit.fixed_probe: observe.py collect/audit checks exact 10 case set, ordinary expected counters, semantic parity and overflow rejection; diagnostic metadata-failure injection and overflow have narrower baseline parity
workload_audit.identity_intervals: registry generation=(base,register sequence); move/swap rebind preserves generation; erase ends generation. Base reuse produces new generation. VM mapping subject reserve->unmap interval is separate; pool cache does not unregister an arena not yet registered, and address can be reused. Allocation origin follows allocation pointer lifetime across move/swap and free, not current Scope. Per-origin-owner raw pointer peak may merge reused base generations; call it raw-identity peak and use generation reconstruction for exclusive lifetime claims. Shared domain2/3/4 allocations are causal, never owner-exclusive.
workload_audit.start: fresh process recorder, resources to be interpreted must be constructed after recording starts. Preexisting registered owners, tracked allocations or prewarmed pools from an unrecorded phase are unsupported. Warm-up can be a recorded Phase whose events are retained. Do not trim/reset trace.
